notes: Stage 8 final boundary register. Public API routes are database queries, database mutations, regulated admission, static/infrastructure delivery or explicit retirement responses. Execution and workspace access belong only to the separate singleton worker. No temporary UI bypass or automatic legacy fallback remains.

static.compatibility: Retain static delivery and Host/Origin defenses; distinguish application reads.

runtime-query.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
runtime-query.effect: Read active runtime and capability state
runtime-query.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
runtime-query.compatibility: Preserve health shape through SQL worker publications, negotiated boundary versions and explicit expiry; API availability is independent of worker readiness.

runtime-control.source: SQL runtime.control intent; worker-owned runtime/drain handles
runtime-control.effect: Accept receipt; independent control consumer performs drain or cancellation
runtime-control.authority: SQL acceptance and worker observation; OS supervisor remains infrastructure
runtime-control.compatibility: Version-1 asynchronous receipt targets an exact worker lifetime; replay cannot drain a replacement. The API never signals or restarts execution.

proof-query.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
proof-query.effect: Read committed historical evidence and current applicability derived from fresh worker observations
proof-query.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
proof-query.compatibility: Preserve entity IDs and historical evidence; use worker observations, no query-time repair.

sql-query.compatibility: Retain response shapes; add consistent watermarks and transactional changes.

sql-mutation.source: SQL metadata and typed command intake for worker-owned changes
sql-mutation.effect: Change domain metadata without solver dispatch
sql-mutation.compatibility: Keep existing semantics and authorization; append changes with same transaction.

solver.source: SQL runs/operations and regulated commands; compatible model/source/continuation preflight retained
solver.effect: Commit domain lineage and command together; worker owns execution
solver.authority: SQL command claims, existing run/operation journals, worker-local driver registry
solver.compatibility: Version-1 receipts; SQL-only model/source/continuation admission. The worker repeats workspace freshness and execution preflight before dispatch; no web dispatcher or runner rendezvous.

control.source: SQL control commands, stop intent, exact attempt/invocation approval records
control.effect: Accept intent and receipt; independent worker consumer signals its handles
control.authority: SQL decisions and command ownership; cancellation fences tool release
control.compatibility: Acceptance is asynchronous and distinct from observation; duplicate intents reuse receipts. No request-thread runner signals.

live-feed.source: SQLite run_events, canonical timeline and run_observation_records
live-feed.effect: Replay/tail committed bounded pages; reset expired cursors to snapshots
live-feed.compatibility: Both run observers qualified; no process-local buffer supplies UI state.

session-feed.source: SQLite domain_changes with snapshot watermarks and durable retention floor
session-feed.effect: Emit cursor-addressed invalidations and explicit expiry resets
session-feed.compatibility: Standalone snapshots before connecting and reconnecting; preserve selected session and presentation.

workspace-read.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
workspace-read.effect: Read file bytes/tree or construct archive/graph
workspace-read.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
workspace-read.compatibility: Backfill immutable bytes and inventories; serve only persisted content/results.

workspace-write.effect: Adapter routes admit worker commands; worker services create/save/move/retire/restore/delete files or projects
workspace-write.authority: SQL command claims, immutable drafts/current bindings, retained before-images, domain preservation services and worker-local guards
workspace-write.compatibility: 202 receipts consumed by supported clients. Only separate worker registrations execute mutations; all public reads and companion state use SQL.

check.effect: Admit checks/rebuilds/verification; compiler work and exact-byte/environment publication execute in workers
check.authority: Filesystem evidence and SQL check records
check.compatibility: Worker check command; distinguish operational completion from Lean verdict.

lsp.source: Immutable SQL buffer and typed editor command
lsp.effect: Admit bounded language analysis; worker owns the private LSP session
lsp.compatibility: No raw JSON-RPC or direct WebSocket. Unsupported widget RPC and other unadapted methods are explicit capability limits.

library.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
library.effect: Read persisted library inventory and explicit observation freshness; no query-triggered refresh or compiler
library.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
library.compatibility: Persist worker inventory and freshness; declaration GET must not compile.

dependency.source: Project dependency DB, reservations, source files and solver workers
dependency.compatibility: Reuse dependency identities; durable child lineage and parent handoff.

review.source: Version-bound SQL review plus current artifact/environment capture
review.effect: Admit a version-bound decision; worker records approval and may apply a retained candidate through the fenced journal
review.compatibility: Pure review reads use DB snapshots; decisions/applications preserve exact revision scope.

reformalization-read.source: SQL operation, receipts, retained versions and drafts
reformalization-read.effect: Read committed state; GET no longer wakes preparation or application
reformalization-read.compatibility: SQL command scheduler owns progress even with no observers. Existing response identities retained.

source-callback.source: Static retirement response; historical accepted source records are read-only
source-callback.effect: Return a static retirement response; no source request is sent to a browser
source-callback.authority: Database publication protocol; reverse callbacks are retired
source-callback.compatibility: Pending/respond callbacks return retirement responses; new work requires an immutable published source reference.

mirror.effect: Publish SQL archive; accepted worker binds it later
mirror.authority: Database archive identity; no request-time workspace materialization
mirror.compatibility: Commit scoped immutable source first; worker materializes without callbacks.

settings.source: SQL policy/preferences and opaque infrastructure credential tickets
settings.effect: Queue policy/credential updates; publish redacted SQL status
settings.authority: Database policy; credential bytes remain in protected infrastructure storage
settings.compatibility: DB application settings and redacted status; separate explicit credential intake exception.

catalog-query.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
catalog-query.effect: Read suggested or effective capabilities from files/runtime
catalog-query.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
catalog-query.compatibility: Persist catalog and effective capability views; no provider/config scan during query.

external.authority: Accepted command and existing domain authorization
external.compatibility: Queue bounded authorized work; retain receipts and never replay uncertain effects blindly.

retired.compatibility: Keep retired; do not recreate independent Lea Check.

companion-query.source: Typed SQL companion command and immutable accepted source bindings
companion-query.effect: Assemble manifest/status/session/job views and synchronize mappings
companion-query.authority: SQL accepted intent and fenced adapter-owned business worker
companion-query.compatibility: Migrate associations; eliminate JSON authority and filesystem fallback.

companion-solver.source: Typed SQL companion command and immutable accepted source bindings
companion-solver.authority: SQL accepted intent and fenced adapter-owned business worker
companion-solver.compatibility: Move prompt/orchestration to worker; retain thin async request translator only.

companion-control.source: Typed SQL companion command and immutable accepted source bindings
companion-control.authority: SQL accepted intent and fenced adapter-owned business worker
companion-control.compatibility: Persist intents and lineage; do not revive JSON writers after cutover.

settings-read.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
settings-read.effect: Read configuration/credential presence and effective settings
settings-read.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
settings-read.compatibility: DB application settings and redacted status; separate explicit credential intake exception.

catalog-install.effect: Read packaged catalog defaults and persist a new installed capability
catalog-install.compatibility: Persist catalog and effective capability views; no provider/config scan during query.

metadata-projection.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
metadata-projection.effect: Update SQL metadata and return a database-only decorated projection
metadata-projection.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
metadata-projection.compatibility: Preserve entity IDs and historical evidence; use worker observations, no query-time repair.

review-query.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
review-query.effect: Read revision-bound review context from retained evidence and worker observations
review-query.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
review-query.compatibility: Pure review reads use DB snapshots; decisions/applications preserve exact revision scope.

companion-feed.effect: Wake extension views after companion state changes
companion-feed.compatibility: Relay durable SQL change cursors and snapshots through the stateless public companion; no JSON job authority.

enrolled-files.caller: Standalone filesystem view and compatible clients
enrolled-files.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
enrolled-files.effect: Read current/historical indexed bytes and tree; explicit synchronization/expiry state
enrolled-files.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
enrolled-files.compatibility: Automatic SQL projection enrollment. Unindexed, expired and over-limit inputs remain explicitly unavailable; no filesystem fallback.

core-projection.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
core-projection.effect: Read persisted proof, review and assessment facts without workspace access or repair
core-projection.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
core-projection.compatibility: Automatic project/loose-session SQL projection enrollment. Unavailable observations disable current-proof and approval claims; no peripheral fallback.

command-intake.source: Strict typed envelope and database policy/capacity records
command-intake.effect: Atomically admit synthetic commands with scoped idempotency and finite quotas
command-intake.authority: Database command registry and authenticated producer
command-intake.compatibility: Synthetic handlers only; no production execution/control family changes in Stage 3.

run-observation.source: SQL history, content bindings and versioned worker observations
run-observation.effect: Read committed progress, control receipt outcomes and recovery availability
run-observation.authority: Database; current claims require fresh observed inputs
run-observation.compatibility: Recovery classification is a retained SQL observation. This GET performs no filesystem preflight, admission, signalling or repair.

workspace-intake.caller: Standalone UI and Overleaf companion through the existing local Host/Origin boundary
workspace-intake.source: Typed versioned arguments, immutable SQL blobs and database revisions
workspace-intake.effect: Admit workspace commands atomically with drafts and finite queue capacity; no filesystem/compiler/provider access
workspace-intake.authority: Server-assigned compatibility producer and SQL command ownership
workspace-intake.compatibility: 202 receipt; legacy routes translate and capture a SQL base when omitted. Versioned edits require an explicit expected_revision.

workspace-query.source: SQL workspace requests, command receipts, immutable blobs and current bindings
workspace-query.effect: Read revision/content, reconcile lost receipts by original idempotency key, and observe results
workspace-query.authority: Committed database records under the existing local security boundary
workspace-query.compatibility: No workspace or live worker lookup. Binary content remains explicitly encoded; command errors are separate from Lean verdicts.

private-worker.caller: Private adapter-owned business worker, live epoch and accepted command required
private-worker.source: SQL companion intent/records and worker workspace observations
private-worker.effect: Execute accepted orchestration and publish SQL results; inaccessible from the public companion
private-worker.authority: Database command generation, worker lease, source bindings and workspace journals
private-worker.compatibility: Private domain handlers run only in the worker-owned business process. Its API calls require SQL-verified parent command, epoch and bridge proof and expose only SQL query/admission operations.

stateless-transport.caller: Overleaf extension and optional compatibility clients
stateless-transport.source: Database API queries, receipts, source publications and change feed
stateless-transport.effect: Translate requests and relay persisted observations; no workspace mount or authoritative local store
stateless-transport.compatibility: Mutating actions pass the original idempotency key through regulated queue intake; immutable source and preferences use SQL-only publication.

workspace-command.source: SQL companion intent/records and worker workspace observations
workspace-command.effect: SQL-only admission; worker executes a typed command
workspace-command.authority: Database command generation, worker lease, source bindings and workspace journals
workspace-command.compatibility: Public contracts register validation only. Execution handlers register only in the separate worker; claims and publications are database fenced.

source-publication.effect: Persist source identity, sequence and file archive atomically; no browser callbacks or workspace access
source-publication.authority: Database publisher generation and immutable content hashes
source-publication.compatibility: Published IDs replace callback snapshots. A changed generation or head requires explicit resubmission.

editor_query.source: SQL published file, editor receipt and bounded result
editor_query.effect: Read persisted versioned language output without execution
editor_query.authority: Database; results are buffer/environment fenced and never proof evidence
editor_query.compatibility: No raw JSON-RPC or direct WebSocket. Unsupported widget RPC and other unadapted methods are explicit capability limits.

editor_buffer.source: Explicit editor-owned immutable bytes or owner registration
editor_buffer.effect: Publish scoped immutable buffer or register a bounded editor producer
editor_buffer.compatibility: No raw JSON-RPC or direct WebSocket. Unsupported widget RPC and other unadapted methods are explicit capability limits.

retired_lsp.effect: Reject every client before accept or execution
retired_lsp.compatibility: Strict cutover. Rollback may disable the editor or select a compliant build; no direct execution fallback.
